notes: Summary: Northcove is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for latency-sensitive trading assistant + real-time reranking. Main ask = tight tail SLOs and clear measurement contract.

Use-case specifics: interactive trading assistant -> sub-100ms p50 target for short prompts; conservative p95/p99 targets for order-of-magnitude decisions. Reranking pipeline requires low-latency first-pass scores and higher-latency full-rankings.

Latency SLOs discussed (initial asks): p50 < 80ms (non-streaming short queries), p95 < 220ms, p99 < 400ms. For streaming/chat flows: p50 time-to-first-token < 40ms, token-emit-rate p95 >= 20 tokens/s.

Measurement alignment items: must agree on 'measurement boundary' — Northcove insists on client-side end-to-end (including TLS + regional network) for SLAs; Redwood prefers server-side for operational SLOs. Recommended approach = dual reporting: server-side primary for operational alerts, client-side as business SLA (with explicit network normalization).

Percentile calculation: discuss HDR histogram vs aggregated sample-percentile. Northcove wants p99 computed on full-request latency (not per-chunk) with minimum sample size per 30d window (>=10k requests) and rejection of cold-start spikes during warm-up.

Streaming vs non-streaming: agree separate SLO buckets. Streaming SLOs defined on time-to-first-byte (TTFB) and sustained token throughput; non-streaming on request-complete latency. Need to standardize 'complete' (e.g., generator EOS vs client cancel).

Client instrumentation: recommend lightweight end-to-end SDK hook (time.request_start, time.first_token, time.last_token). Proposal: Redwood provide canonical client-side metric names and aggregation script for parity checks.

SLA negotiation points to raise: measurement window (30d rolling), minimum sample thresholds, warm-up exclusion (first 72h of deployment), remediation credits structure (tiered per % breach), joint incident RCA within 5 business days, allowed fallback to lower-capacity model during infra incidents.

Reserved GPU planning notes: baseline QPS estimate = 60 req/s for core reranking flow (avg prompt 1.2k tokens). Recommend reserved pool sized for steady-state + 30% headroom for bursts; pre-warm KV cache instances to avoid tail spikes. Consider 2-tier pool: guaranteed capacity + burst-on-demand.

Throughput guarantees: Redwood proposed per-GPU modeled throughput numbers; Northcove asked for validated 95th-percentile throughput for their prompt mix (producer to run production replay). Action: Redwood to run replay and produce per-GPU throughput profile and recommended pool size.

Admission control & graceful degradation: design requirement = protect p99 for high-priority requests. Suggest policies: request prioritization, dynamic batching caps, and auto-fallback rules to smaller model variant with clear fidelity degradation messaging in responses.

Observability & proofs: Northcove requires token-level cost/latency breakdown, traceable request-id across client->gateway->runtime, and access to per-route percentile dashboards during trial. Ask: 90-day retention on trace slices for postmortem.
Quote from call: 'If we can't measure it the same way, we can't sign.' — Head of Infrastructure. Need explicit contract language aligning definitions.
